senses.label: Distress as a passion
senses.summary: Disturbance of the mind is a passion arising from judgement, not a bodily load.
markers: disturbance arises from one's own judgements

sources.note: Perturbationes animi: the Stoic classification of passions.

senses.label: Stress as a bodily response
senses.summary: Any demand on the body triggers a general physiological stress response; prolonged, it causes illness.
markers: the body mounts a general physical response to any demand
hazards: The word 'stress' alone is left out: older English used it for hardship and pressure. Markers carry the modern sense.

sources.citation: Hans Selye, 'A syndrome produced by diverse nocuous agents', Nature (1936)

senses.label: Stress management
senses.summary: Stress is reduced by learned coping techniques, often taught by professionals or employers.
markers: stress can be reduced with techniques taught by professionals

sources.citation: Lazarus and Folkman, Stress, Appraisal, and Coping (1984)
sources.note: The coping framework; stress-management programmes spread from the 1970s.
